title: Suspicious activity reporting
definition: The requirement to file a report on transactions conducted, or attempted, that are suspicious by the institution's judgement, subject to a stated reporting threshold. For covered institutions the threshold is set by reference to the amount involved and to whether the transaction has an apparent lawful purpose, and a continuing-activity rule requires a further report while the activity continues. This record summarises the obligation; the thresholds and the applicable rules are set out in the source.
evidence_to_cite: the filed report, its identifier and the period it covers
the transaction records the report was based on
the basis for the suspicion, as recorded at the time

sources.citation: Suspicious activity reporting requirements for banks (31 CFR 1020.320), summarised in the FinCrime regulatory index.

notes: The decision to report is a judgement the institution makes and documents, not a computation. The record of that judgement is what has to be evidenced.
